title: Predoctoral Training in Translational Immunology
text:
This new program seeks to train pre-doctoral students to better recognize how to translate scientific
discoveries in immunology to influence and improve the health of patients with cancer, autoimmunity and
infectious diseases.

title: [18F]F-AraG as an imaging biomarker for early diagnosis and monitoring of cardiotoxicity related to doxorubicin and immune check point inhibitor therapy
text:
(Relevance)
The development of an imaging method for early detection of cardiotoxicity associated with cancer therapy is
crucial for prevention and better management of cardiac complications in cancer patients and survivors. This
technique would allow optimization of cancer therapy, help prevent serious cardiovascular problems, and lead
to improved quality of life. In addition, this method could lead to development of new treatments for heart disease
and heart-safe cancer therapies.

title: T Cell-Specific BRCA1 Function in Antitumor Immunity and Immunotherapy
text:
By combining the awesome power of mouse genetics, precious clinical samples, and cutting-edge
technologies, this multidisciplinary team is poised to illuminate a novel function of T cell-specific BRCA1 in
antitumor immunity, immunotherapy, and transcriptional regulation. The proposed work promises to have a far-
reaching conceptual and translational impact on the current understanding of BRCA1 tumor suppressor function
and development of new cancer prevention options for BRCA1 mutation carriers.

title: Metabolism Core
text: “Metabolomics” largely consists of metabolic profiling, which is the process of identification and quantification of a large number of metabolites of many different biochemical classes, from diverse biological samples, including cells, culture media, tissue and biofluids. However, to understand the metabolic underpinning of diseases such as cancer, biochemical mechanism(s) must be elucidated, in which case it is necessary to introduce appropriate stable isotope tracers. Although this greatly increases the number of analytes to be quantified, it also enables the retrieval of much more biologically relevant information. This Stable Isotope Resolved Metabolomics (SIRM) approach is a unique specialty of the Metabolism Core, led by PIs with over 40 years of combined expertise in SIRM. The goals of the Metabolism Core are to provide services for a wide coverage of the metabolome with isotopomer and isotopologue analysis, and high throughput protein analysis. To achieve this, we make use of four major analytical platforms, namely (1) high resolution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), (2) ultra-high resolution Fourier-transform mass spectrometry (UHR-FTMS), with or without chromatography, (3) ultra-trace elemental analyses by inductively-coupled plasma MS (ICPMS), and (4) Reverse Phase Protein Arrays (RPPA). The Metabolism Core personnel will advise on analytical methods and SIRM-based experimental design with development of additional techniques to address specific issues of identification and quantification and biological interpretation relevant to the COBRE Projects. Because experimental design and sample preparation are integral to the data acquisition and interpretation, the Metabolism Core provides expertise in these and informatics relevant to the SIRM approach. These goals will be achieved according to the following Specific Aims. Specific Aim 1. To provide access and expertise across a wide range of NMR, MS and RPPA technologies to investigators. Specific Aim 2. To provide experimental design, sample processing, and support to the investigators for data reduction, metabolic pathway, and biochemical mechanism analyses. Specific Aim 3. To develop and implement new methods to enhance metabolic capabilities relevant to the COBRE Projects. This Core will support the young investigators by providing advanced analytical technologies and expertise in the metabolic requirements for cancer development and behavior.

title: Genomics of rapid adaptation in the lab and in the wild
text:
Evolutionary adaptation is the core concept in biology and is at the center of many problems facing humanity
such as cancer and infectious disease. The Petrov Lab will pursue a series of interrelated project to infer
patterns and process of evolutionary adaptation from historical data and studying evolution in action.

title: Restoring T-cell Immunity in Older Adults with Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Thymic Epithelial Cells
text:
The thymus is essential for lifelong T cell development, but thymic epithelial cells (TECs), the key
cellular component of the thymic microenvironment, undergo progressive functional and numerical decline with
age. This loss leads to thymic involution/atrophy, reduced T cell output, and immunodeficiency in older adults,
resulting in heightened susceptibility to infection, diminished vaccine responsiveness, and increased cancer
risk. This project will define the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing differentiation of mouse
embryonic stem cells (mESCs) into thymic epithelial progenitors (TEPs) and TECs and investigate the ability of
human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) from somatic cells of older adults to develop into TEPs/TECs to
support T cell development from co-transplanted human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) in aged mice.

title: Integration of High-Precision Tunable Laser Spectroscopy (HPTLS) into Liquid Chromatography for Quantitative Bioformulation Analysis
text:
Manufacturing biopharmaceuticals requires careful control of product composition, including the active
pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and supporting excipients that ensure stability, safety, and effectiveness. To
confirm this control, manufacturers rely heavily on liquid chromatography (LC), a gold-standard method for
separating product components. However, LC often requires multiple detectors or follow-up assays to achieve
accurate identification and quantification, leading to long turnaround times, higher costs, and increased risk of
delays in delivering life-saving therapies. Nirrin Technologies has developed the ATLAS-Flow system, which uses
High-Precision Tunable Laser Spectroscopy (HPTLS) to provide rapid, direct quantitation of proteins, nucleic
acids, sugars, amino acids, and surfactants without the need for sample preparation.

title: Mechanisms for activation of beige adipose tissue in humans
text:
This research grant is designed to determine whether chronic treatment with mirabegron, a β3
adrenergic receptor agonist approved for treatment of over active bladder, improves metabolic
homeostasis in prediabetic, obese, research participants. We will also investigate the
underlying mechanisms for improved β-cell function and insulin sensitivity by mirabegron
treatment, which we recently demonstrated. There is a tremendous need for new approaches
to fight the obesity and type 2 diabetes epidemic, and this research is thus highly relevant to
human health.

title: Investigating the role of A20 and DREAM in adipogenesis and systemic sclerosis
text:
In this project we will investigate mechanisms of how A20 promotes adipogenesis and the absence/low A20 in
scleroderma (SSc) patients will cause transdifferentiation of adipocytes to mesenchymal phenotype in SSc
thereby initiating fibrosis. Furthermore, A20 suppressor DREAM is elevated and anti-correlated to A20 in SSc
patients. We are going to study whether blocking DREAM function can restore A20 levels/activity and reduce
fibrotic phenotypes in SSc.

title: Two-photon Imaging of Oxygen and Blood Flow in Retinal and Cerebral Vasculature
text:
High-resolution imaging techniques are essential for investigation of the pathogenesis and development of
therapeutic and screening strategies for cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), including Alzheimer Disease (AD)
and AD-related dementias. We propose to develop novel methods to investigate retinal O2 delivery and
consumption with unprecedented spatial resolution and to correlate changes that occur in parallel in retinal and
cortical microvasculature during normal ageing and AD. We hope that this work will advance our understanding
of the concurrent microvascular dysfunction in cortex and retina during both normal ageing and SVD progression,
provide broad utility in assessing retinal microvascular domains in animal models of eye disorders, and augment
knowledge of vascular mechanisms of progressive neurodegeneration and cognitive impairment in common
forms of SVD as well as in AD and related dementias.

title: Preclinical Genome Editing for Rare Neurological Diseases
text:
TO PUBLIC HEALTH
Science and medicine have revolutionized our ability to diagnose rare genetic diseases, but patients and their
families still have vanishingly limited treatment options. This is because of the challenges in precisely correcting
genetic diseases using gene therapies that are both safe and effective. This U19 program seeks to address this
vexing gap for four neurological conditions, with the goal of bringing at least one gene-editing therapeutic to the
FDA within 5 years. Success in our program could revolutionize treatment for at least one of the conditions we
will study and pave the path for the others in the near future.

title: Identifying HIV treatment engagement factors using clinical informatics and stated preference methods
text:
Despite advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART), many people with HIV (PWH) experience treatment-
adherence challenges, leading to suboptimal outcomes and limiting progress toward ending the HIV epidemic.
Existing clinical decision support (CDS) tools rarely incorporate rich patient-reported preferences or
unstructured electronic health record (EHR) notes, missing opportunities to personalize care. This project will
provide advanced training and develop a patient-informed CDS prototype that integrates natural language
processing (NLP)-derived insights from EHR notes with patient-reported preferences to generate tailored
suggested actions, which will be user-tested in a nonclinical, vignette-based study for acceptability, usability,
and intended adoption, ultimately improving adherence and health outcomes for PWH.

title: Therapeutic and Mechanistic Insights in Food Allergy
text:
Daily maintenance dosing during oral immunotherapy (OIT) for food allergy and the risk of comorbid
eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) are major burdens for food allergic individuals. Here we propose to reduce
these burdens by determining the safety and efficacy of high concentration reduced-frequency OIT
maintenance dosing regimens (network-wide project). Furthermore, we will characterize gastrointestinal
features of food allergic individuals with and without EoE (CRC-specific project).

title: Cellular senescence contributes to salivary gland dysfunction in Sjögren’s syndrome
text:
Sjӧgren’s syndrome-associated xerostomia significantly reduces the oral health and overall quality of life of 2-4
million Americans. Currently, no known cure or effective treatments exist for Sjӧgren’s syndrome. Completion of
this study will provide a critical and rational foundation for the development of effective interventions targeting
senescent cells to combat this disorder.

title: Neocortical and Hippocampal Circuit Dysfunction in the KCNT1 Model of Epilepsy
text:
Mutation of the KCNT1 gene encoding for Slack channels is associated with multiple pediatric epilepsies and
intellectual impairment. The proposed project will test the hypothesis that hypoexcitability of somatostatin positive
interneurons, and ensuing disinhibition of a key corticohippocampal neural circuit, is the primary cause of disease
related focal and generalized hypersynchrony. We will also test the hypothesis that optogenetically driving the
activity of these interneurons at frequencies they can sustain, despite having slack channel mutations, could
rectify circuit hypersynchrony in this novel model of developmental epileptic encephalopathy.

title: Maternal mHealth blood hemoglobin analysis with informed deep learning
text:
Anemia, defined by low hemoglobin content in the blood, is common in pregnancy, impairing the health of the
mother as well as babies. Although the condition can easily be treated with currently available supplements or
infusions, anemia is detected too late or not at all. This research focuses on developing a mobile health
technology to simply measure blood hemoglobin levels using digital photos of the eyelid, maximizing the
currently available resources for anemia diagnosis and management during pregnancy, in particular in the
developing world and resource-limited (or at-home) settings.

title: Early identification of immunotherapy resistance through integrated multiparameter imaging
text: The majority of cancer patients who receive immunotherapy do not respond, and rapid determination of who is not responding and why remains an unmet need. Non-invasive imaging methods to monitor early response to immunotherapy and identify mechanisms of resistance would enable rapid and rational adaptation of immunotherapy, improving outcomes for many patients. In this project, we will further develop and test imaging strategies to measure key molecules and cells that govern response and resistance, intervening when these mechanisms are detected to drive stronger immune responses and thus improve outcomes.

title: Developing PARP-1 PET with companion tissue assay as a precision tool to guide PARPi therapy
text:
We will develop a paired imaging/tissue biomarker of sensitivity to PARP inhibitors (PARPi) that can be used for
patient selection, visualization of drug-target engagement, and potentially long-term dose modulation. In breast
cancer, where PARPi are currently used largely in the setting of metastatic disease, the ability to predict response
would also provide a critically needed tool to stratify patients for clinical trials testing neoadjuvant PARPi
therapy/therapy combinations. If successful, this research could lead to a new way to functionally characterize
PARP-1 expressing cancer, guide targeted therapy, and assess therapeutic response and resistance.

title: The role of extracellular vesicle-associated MicroRNAs in HIV-associated atherosclerosis
text:
We have discovered that plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) isolated from people living with
HIV (PLWH) recapitulate the effects of HIV positivity on the development of HIV-associated
cardiovascular disease (CVD) and the potential EV-associated miRNAs (EV-miRs) that mediate this
effect. In this proposal, we will use novel tailored EVs generated by genetic modification of bone
marrow mesenchymal stromal cells to determine if targeting these candidate EV-miRs will abrogate the
effects of HIV positivity in the CVS and characterize the underlying molecular mechanisms/pathways
whereby EVs/TEVs effect atherogenesis.

title: Mobile microscopy for rapid diagnosis of parasitic diseases in refugee settlements
text: Wastewater-associated parasitic infections (e.g. Ascaris, hookworm) threaten vulnerable, rural, and disaster-affected U.S. communities with failing septic infrastructure or contaminated water supplies, creating a need for simple, field-deployable tools that can detect parasitic contamination without centralized laboratories. Because naturally contaminated wastewater containing parasitic worm eggs is not readily available in the United States, this project will use the unique highprevalence wastewater environment and parasitology expertise in Bangladesh to develop and validate an AI-based mobile microscope, the NTDscope, under realistic field conditions. The resulting protocols and technology will provide a new tool for detecting parasites that will be directly deployable by U.S. public health agencies for rural septic monitoring, agricultural water safety, and post-disaster recovery.
